title: Vanguard commitments onepager — Q2 2026 (WIP)
content:
Context and intent:
This file is the working one-pager for the company-wide commitments we want to present at the Q2 all-hands and to use as the basis for the exec update (Mar 25). Purpose: distill cross-team asks, surface known risks, and land measurable OKR drafts that can be iterated in the next two weeks with product/eng leads.

High-level thesis (two lines):
- Focus the company on 3 program-level commitments that together improve customer experience and unit economics: (1) Predictable latency under load, (2) 30% lower serving cost for standard workloads, (3) Enterprise-grade private deploy onboarding.
- Use a single playbook (this doc) to coordinate rollouts, staffing, and the all-hands narrative so teams have clear asks and acceptance criteria.

Program commitments (short):
1) Latency resilience: hold p95 < 120ms for hosted tier at 90% traffic by end of Q2.
2) Cost wins: reduce per-token infra cost 30% for typical low-burst web workloads via batching + cache + quantization profiles.
3) Private onboarding: deliver a hardened private control-plane beta with KMS/HSM integration and audit logging for 3 pilot customers.

Draft OKRs (company-level) — initial numbers are placeholders, expect revision: 
O1: Make Redwood inference predictable for production apps
KR1.1: p95 inference latency < 120ms for 90% of hosted API traffic (baseline: 180ms)
KR1.2: Incident MTTR for inference infra (sev>=2) < 25m (baseline: 48m)
KR1.3: 99.9% availability for hosted model endpoints (monthly SLA telemetry)
Owners: eng-sre (Sasha Kim), serving-runtime (Ethan Clarke)

O2: Improve economics for standard text workloads
KR2.1: Reduce average per-token cost (infra only) by 30% for the top 50% of customer requests by Q2 end
KR2.2: Deploy two quantization profiles and validate accuracy regressions < 2% on production prompts
KR2.3: Launch batching/default cache config suggestions in Redwood Console and have 25 customers adopt in Q2
Owners: optimize (Miguel Ortega), console-and-tooling (Dana Liu)

O3: Launch Private beta with enterprise controls
KR3.1: Ship private control-plane beta with KMS/HSM plugin + audit events to S3 for 3 pilot customers
KR3.2: Create onboarding runbook and automated smoke tests; achieve 3 successful pilot deployments with <3 days install time
KR3.3: Customer satisfaction (CSAT) >= 8/10 from pilot cohort
Owners: private-deployments (Noah Patel), solutions-engineering (Priya Nair)

Cross-functional asks (what teams need to do) — terse:
- Eng: prioritize INFR-1423 (request routing changes) and PROD-2567 (KV-cache persistence); plan two 48-hr performance windows in April and May.
- SRE: finalize rollback playbook + automated canary with traffic-splitting for model rollouts; own MTTR KR telemetry.
- Console: ship console suggestions for batching and a rollout UI for quant profiles; instrument adoption events.
- Solutions/CS: recruit 3 private pilot customers, coordinate legal/compliance checklist, and prepare pilot SOW template.
- GTM: prepare customer messaging + pricing options for private and dedicated offerings; draft enterprise brief for pilot companies.

All-hands run of show (Mar 25) — 45 minutes + 30 min breakouts
- Pre-read (sent 72h prior): one-pager (this doc), two data charts (latency distribution, per-token cost curve), short pilot prospect list.
- 0:00–0:05 — CEO opening: context & northstar (why this matters to roadmap).
- 0:05–0:20 — Product + Eng: state of platform (latency/cost telemetry highlights), three program commitments with top-level KRs.
- 0:20–0:30 — SRE/Infra: outage learnings and MTTR playbook preview.
- 0:30–0:40 — Solutions/CS: private beta ask (what we need: seats, SOW, compliance).
- 0:40–0:45 — Executive ask: company-level decisions (see decision log below).
- Breakouts (30m): focused tracks (infra readiness, console adoption, private pilot logistics).
- Post-event: 72-hr follow-up with action tracker and owners.

Stakeholder matrix (quick):
- Exec: CEO (A), CTO (R), CFO (C) — approve asks with budget delta < $250k.
- Product leads: own KR scoping and acceptance (Ethan, Miguel).
- Eng leads: implement; require SRE support (Sasha).

Major dependencies and blockers: 
- Capacity: Dedicated pool reservation timelines are long — procurement for Q2 burst capacity needs finance sign-off (ticket OP-4123).
- Observability gaps: token-level attribution for multi-tenant workloads is incomplete (tracking PR #2668). Need console instrumentation before we can claim adoption metrics.
- Compliance: KMS integration spec still being finalized (linked Confluence page). Without HSM work, some pilot prospects will delay.

Decision log (to finalize at exec sync on Mar 18):
- D1: Approve $150k temporary burst reserve for April perf window (yes/no) — proposed by Eng.
- D2: Default quantization profile rollout strategy (opt-in vs opt-out) — proposed by Product.
- D3: Pilot customer SLAs for private beta (what are we willing to guarantee?) — proposed by Sales/Legal.

Risk register (headline):
- Accuracy regressions from quantization: medium — mitigation: multi-stage evals + canary prompts and quick rollback recipes.
- Missed telemetry deadlines -> inability to measure KR2 and KR1: high — mitigation: 2-week instrumentation spike priority.
- Pilot delays due to compliance: medium-high — mitigation: prioritize KMS/HSM and provide interim manual audit extracts.

Open questions (notes to self / for leads):
- What is the minimum traffic sample size to meaningfully measure p95 (SRE input).
- If we hit a 25% cost reduction but regress accuracy 2.5% on corner-case prompts, do we accept? (decision needed).
- Finance: is $150k one-time burst reserve acceptable as operating budget or should we reclassify as capital? (CFO ask).

Execution cadence and milestones (short timeline):
- Mar 18: exec decisions on D1–D3; finalize all-hands narrative.
- Mar 25: all-hands + breakouts.
- Apr 6–7: first perf window (48 hrs) — baseline + changes.
- Apr 20–24: instrumentation sprint for console events.
- May 10–May 28: private pilot onboarding (pilot 1, 2, 3).
- Jun 25: end-of-quarter telemetry review and OKR retro.

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Priya: consolidate pilot prospect shortlist and SOW template (due Mar 12).
- Ethan: draft experiment plan for April perf window, include rollback runbook (due Mar 15).
- Sasha: own MTTR baseline report and define required alerting changes (due Mar 16).
- Miguel/Dana: prototype console adoption flow; sketch UI and event schema (due Mar 18).
- Noah: draft private-deploy beta onboarding runbook and install checklist (due Mar 22).

Notes / drafting log (informal):
- Trying to keep the narrative short; execs prefer crisp asks not long encyclopedias.
- Will convert the KR numbers into OKR doc on Confluence after D1–D3.
- Expect pushback from product on the 30% cost target — it may be too aggressive for some model families; prepare a fallback target (20%) and rationale.

References and artifacts to read before sync:
- latency distribution chart (attached in pre-read PPT).
- PR #2668 (console token-adoption instrumentation) — contains the event schema.
- INFR-1423 (routing improvements) and OP-4123 (budget request).

Unassigned / backlog ideas (for later quarters):
- Expand model catalog with verified quant profiles per architecture family.
- Automated quality guardrails tied to prompt regression alerts in Redwood Optimize.
- Self-serve private onboarding experience (beyond pilot).

If you see anything missing in this one-pager — add notes in the comments thread in #company-allhands or tag me directly (Priya). I will iterate and upload the cleaned pre-read by Mar 22 (final pre-read 72h before all-hands).

-- Priya
